stem: A client has complex discharge needs involving mobility limitations, medication management, and difficulty obtaining food at home. Which nursing action best supports coordinated care?

options.A: Arrange collaboration among the relevant disciplines to address the client's identified needs
options.B: Ask each discipline to work independently without sharing significant client information
options.C: Delay collaboration until after the client has been discharged
options.D: Limit planning to nursing concerns even when other disciplines are needed

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes identifying the need for interdisciplinary conferences, reporting significant information to other disciplines, reviewing the plan of care for continuity, and collaborating with multidisciplinary team members. A client with mobility, medication, and food-access needs benefits from coordinated input from relevant disciplines. Working in isolation, delaying collaboration, or restricting the plan to nursing alone does not support continuity of care.
educational_objective: Coordinate complex client needs by collaborating with the appropriate multidisciplinary team members and sharing significant care information.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Replaced low-yield consultative-versus-democratic leadership terminology with an applied interdisciplinary-care coordination item directly mapped to NCSBN 2026 Management of Care.
audit_findings: A directly reflects the listed NCSBN collaboration activities. B prevents communication and continuity, C delays needed planning, and D excludes disciplines despite needs outside nursing alone. The stem contains multiple clearly relevant needs, making interdisciplinary collaboration the single best answer without requiring assumptions about a specific facility structure.
